thread:
Sam (CEO): Thanks for the great questions today. Opening this thread for any follow-ups on mission/positioning. Keep them short and we9ll triage.
Priya (Head of Strategy): Quick one: when a prospect asks, "are you a hosting provider or a serving company?" what's the clean line we should use?
Marcus (Product): Say: "We9re an inference platform: we make models reliable and economical in production, whether you run with us or in your own datacenter."
Lila (Marketing): Can we shorten that to two lines for the website?
Sam (CEO): Website: "Redwood Inference: predictable latency, transparent costs, and production-grade controls for LLMs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
Jonah (Customer Success): Customers keep asking about migration effort. Any standard quote?
Priya (Head of Strategy): Use: "Start on hosted and scale to Dedicated or Private with the same API semantics; some infra work required for private installs but we provide tooling and docs."
Marcus (Product): Tactically add: model & config versioning + canary rollouts reduce migration risk.
Lila (Marketing): On competitors: should we name clouds (GH/CloudX) or keep it generic in public materials?
Sam (CEO): Keep public comms outcome-focused: "vs managed endpoints" and "vs self-hosted runtimes". Internally map to specifics in sales playbooks.
Jonah (Customer Success): Prospect asked about unit economics. Any crisp rule of thumb for hosted vs dedicated?
Marcus (Product): Rough: if you9re under X tokens/day and highly variable, hosted is faster and cheaper. If you9re running sustained heavy throughput, dedicated reserved capacity typically gives much lower $/token. We9ll add a concrete example to the playbook.
Priya (Head of Strategy): Market question: are we explicitly targeting platform teams at mid-market or pushing enterprise first?
Sam (CEO): Our go-to-market is PLG-first but with clear escalation to enterprise motions for Dedicated/Private once usage or security needs hit thresholds.
Lila (Marketing): For messaging: emphasize predictable ops + choice. That resonates in both segments.
Jonah (Customer Success): Any guidance on handling RFPs where customers list multiple inference vendors?
Marcus (Product): Point them to our SLA, audit logs, and the rollout story. Also provide a short eval kit: latency/cost scripts and a small prompt suite.
Priya (Head of Strategy): Happy to own a 1-page "why Redwood" with bullets for sales engineering.
Sam (CEO): Perfect. Priya take lead, Marcus add the tech bullets, Lila craft the header. Jonah share 1-2 customer questions you see often. OpsBot: Recording + transcript uploaded: https://redwood.company/records/all-hands/1854321111 :white_check_mark:
Lila (Marketing): Will draft and ping #sales for review.
Marcus (Product): Adding kernel/quantization impacts to the doc.
Jonah (Customer Success): I9ll attach two RFP snippets we've seen.
Sam (CEO): Thanks team 1: let9s get this in the playbook before next week.
Priya (Head of Strategy): Will share draft in #strategy by EOD.
Lila (Marketing): Adding two headline options for A/B test.
Marcus (Product): If anyone wants cost numbers for examples, DM me.
Jonah (Customer Success): Thanks all!
